summary: Source decomposition of the parts of the integral Iwasawa programme for which primary sources were actually readable: Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams Sec. 13.4 (read in full) for the cyclotomic-tower class-field-theory sequence, the control statement and the Vandiver collapse; Dasgupta-Kakde-Silliman-Wang's introduction (read in full) for the generalised Ritter-Weiss modules, the conditions (A1)-(A5), the quadratic presentation, the keystone Fitting-ideal theorem with its explicit 2^t normalisation and the Brumer-Stark conclusion; and Kurihara Secs. 2.6 and 4 for the (S,T) form of the keystone theorem, the compactly supported Iwasawa complex with its Selmer comparison, and the equivariant main conjecture Det(RGamma_c)^{-1} = g Lambda INCLUDING p = 2. Two structural points are recorded with their sources: the minus construction is the QUOTIENT Z[G]/(1+c) and not an eigenspace or an idempotent summand, which is what makes the p = 2 statements meaningful; and Kurihara's Lemma 4.2(1) is an isomorphism only for p > 2, with a cokernel of order 2 at p = 2 whose cohomological source is H^1(Delta', Q_p/Z_p) = Z/2Z. This packet covers 6 of the 20 stages with nodes. THE OTHER 14 ARE MARKED not_read OR partial WITH NO NODES, and three of them are blocked by missing sources: Mazur-Wiles is present but has no text layer, Wiles's totally real paper and Ferrero-Washington and Washington's book are absent from the library. The five KU-prefixed aggregate stages were not worked because their prerequisites lie in eight roadmaps outside EXT-15.

nodes.title: The four-term exact sequence relating global units, semilocal units, the p-ramified group and the class groups
nodes.statement: Let F_n be the real cyclotomic fields, U_n the local units and U_{n,1} the principal ones, V_n = O_{F_n}^x the global units, E_n the p-adic closure of V_n inside U_n, E_n^+ = E_n intersect U_n^+, E_{n,1} = E_n intersect U_{n,1}, E_{n,1}^+ = E_n^+ intersect U_{n,1}, and E_{infinity,1}^+ = lim E_{n,1}^+. PROPOSITION 13.13: global class field theory gives, at each finite level, a short exact sequence 0 -> E_{n,1}^+ -> U_{n,1}^+ -> Gal(M_n^+/L_n^+) -> 0; taking the inverse limit over n gives 0 -> E_{infinity,1}^+ -> U_{infinity,1}^+ -> Gal(M_infinity^+/L_infinity^+) -> 0, EXACTNESS IN THE LIMIT being justified because all three modules are finitely generated Z_p-modules and therefore satisfy the Mittag-Leffler condition. COROLLARY 13.14: combining this with the tautological short exact sequence 0 -> Gal(M_infinity^+/L_infinity^+) -> X_infinity^+ -> Y_infinity^+ -> 0 supplied by the fundamental theorem of Galois theory, and with the third isomorphism theorem in the form Gal(M_infinity^+/L_infinity^+) = (E_{infinity,1}^+/U_{infinity,1}^+) = (E_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+)/(U_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+), one obtains the four-term exact sequence of Lambda(G)-modules 0 -> E_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ -> U_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ -> X_infinity^+ -> Y_infinity^+ -> 0.
hypotheses: M_infinity is the maximal abelian p-extension of L_infinity unramified outside p and L_infinity is the maximal unramified abelian p-extension, so X_infinity = Gal(M_infinity/L_infinity-base) and Y_infinity = Gal(L_infinity/F_infinity) are DIFFERENT modules classifying different extensions; they are not interchangeable in a main conjecture
the passage to the inverse limit is exact only because all the modules are finitely generated over Z_p (the Mittag-Leffler condition); this is stated explicitly and is not automatic
the units appearing are the PRINCIPAL local units U_{n,1} and the corresponding closures E_{n,1}, not the full unit groups; the plus superscripts are the totally real parts
Leopoldt's conjecture for the F_n is used to know that E_n is a finite Z_p-module of rank r_1 + r_2 - 1 = p^{n-1}(p-1)/2; it is known in this case by a theorem of Brumer
the quotient in the middle is U/E, not E/U
proofSteps: Global class field theory (Washington Cor. 13.6) gives the finite-level sequence (13.1).
Take the inverse limit, exact by Mittag-Leffler.

Apply the fundamental theorem of Galois theory to get the short exact sequence with X_infinity^+ and Y_infinity^+, and the third isomorphism theorem to rewrite Gal(M_infinity^+/L_infinity^+) as the quotient of the two unit quotients.
Splice the two sequences.
acceptance: Check the distinction between X_infinity^+ (p-ramified) and Y_infinity^+ (unramified) at every use.
Check that the exactness of the inverse limit is justified by finite generation over Z_p, and that Leopoldt (via Brumer) is what gives the rank of E_n.
Check the direction of the middle quotient: it is U/E and not E/U.

Check the Lambda(Gamma)-action: by Remark 13.7 it is defined by sigma . x = sigma-tilde x sigma-tilde^{-1} for any lift sigma-tilde, well defined and extended by continuity because O_L[Gamma] is dense in Lambda(Gamma) and the latter is Hausdorff.

sources.excerpt: Proposition 13.13. There is an exact sequence of Lambda(Gamma^+)-modules 0 -> E^+_{infinity,1} -> U^+_{infinity,1} -> Gal(M^+_infinity/L^+_infinity) -> 0. Proof. Global class field theory (see [Was97, Cor. 13.6]) gives a short exact sequence 0 -> E^+_{n,1} -> U^+_{n,1} -> Gal(M_n^+/L_n^+) -> 0. (13.1) Taking the inverse limit over n gives the result. This is exact as all modules in the sequence above are finitely generated Z_p-modules (so satisfy the Mittag-Leffler condition).
sources.match: Gives the finite-level sequence, the limit, and the exactness justification recorded in the hypotheses.

sources.locator: Sec. 13.4, Cor. 13.14 with its proof, printed p. 68
sources.excerpt: Corollary 13.14. We have an exact sequence of Lambda(G)-modules 0 -> E^+_{infinity,1}/C^+_{infinity,1} -> U^+_{infinity,1}/C^+_{infinity,1} -> X^+_infinity -> Y^+_infinity -> 0. Proof. The fundamental theorem of Galois theory yields a short exact sequence 0 -> Gal(M^+_infinity/L^+_infinity) -> X^+_infinity -> Y^+_infinity -> 0. The result now follows from Proposition 13.13, as Gal(M^+_infinity/L^+_infinity) = (E^+_{infinity,1}/U^+_{infinity,1}) = (E^+_{infinity,1}/C^+_{infinity,1})/(U^+_{infinity,1}/C^+_{infinity,1}), the last identification being the third isomorphism theorem.
sources.match: Gives the four-term sequence and the exact splicing argument.

sources.locator: Sec. 13.4, Def. 13.12 and the paragraph after it, printed p. 67
sources.excerpt: Definition 13.12. For any n >= 1, define E_n as the p-adic closure of the global units V_n = O_{F_n}^x inside the local units U_n, let E_n^+ := E_n intersect U_n^+, and let E_{n,1} := E_n intersect U_{n,1}, E^+_{n,1} := E_n^+ intersect U_{n,1}; E_{infinity,1} := lim E_{n,1}, E^+_{infinity,1} = lim E^+_{n,1}. Leopoldt's conjecture (which is known in this case by a theorem of Brumer) states that for any n >= 1, the group E_n is a finite Z_p-module of rank r_1 + r_2 - 1 = p^{n-1}(p-1)/2.
sources.match: Gives the exact definitions of all the unit modules and records the Leopoldt/Brumer input.

nodes.title: The control statement (Y_infinity^+)_{Gamma_n^+} = Y_n^+ and its use
nodes.statement: With Y_n^+ = Gal(L_n^+/F_n^+), which class field theory identifies with Cl(F_n^+) tensor_Z Z_p, and Gamma_n^+ = Gal(F_infinity^+/F_n^+), one has for all n >= 0 the identification of COINVARIANTS (Y_infinity^+)_{Gamma_n^+} = Y_n^+. This is the control statement quoted by Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams as Washington Prop. 13.22, with their own proof given in their Appendix A (Prop. A.6). It is the mechanism that converts a statement about the Iwasawa module Y_infinity^+ into statements about the finite-level class groups, and it is what makes Nakayama's lemma applicable: knowing Y_1^+ = 0 gives (Y_infinity^+)_{Gamma_0^+} = 0 and hence Y_infinity^+ = 0.
hypotheses: the identification is with the module of COINVARIANTS, not the invariants; the left-hand side is (Y_infinity^+)_{Gamma_n^+}
Y_n^+ is identified with Cl(F_n^+) tensor Z_p by class field theory -- the identification (13.2) -- so the control statement is simultaneously a statement about class groups and about Galois groups

the statement as quoted is for the totally real cyclotomic tower, which is totally ramified at the unique prime above p; the general Z_p-extension version requires the eventual-ramification analysis that the stage text asks for separately
Nakayama's lemma applies because Y_infinity^+ is a finitely generated Lambda-module and Gamma_0^+ is procyclic
proofSteps: Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams quote the statement from Washington and refer to their own Appendix A for a proof; the appendix was NOT read here.

The application in Cor. 13.16(i) runs: if p does not divide h_1^+ then by (13.2) Y_1^+ = 0, so by the control statement 0 = Y_1^+ = (Y_infinity^+)_{Gamma_0^+}, and Nakayama's lemma gives Y_infinity^+ = 0.
Part (ii) then reverses the implication at every level: Y_n^+ = 0 for all n, hence p does not divide h_n^+ for any n.
acceptance: Check that the argument in Cor. 13.16(i) is genuinely TWO steps -- first Y_1^+ = 0 from the class-number hypothesis via (13.2), then Y_infinity^+ = 0 by Nakayama -- and not a single application of the control statement.
Check the coinvariants-versus-invariants direction.
Check the identification Y_n^+ = Cl(F_n^+) tensor Z_p, which is what makes p not dividing h_n^+ equivalent to Y_n^+ = 0.
Check that the general Z_p-extension version requires additional ramification control, which this statement does not supply.

sources.locator: Sec. 13.4, Cor. 13.16 with proof, printed p. 68
sources.excerpt: Corollary 13.16. If p is a Vandiver prime, then: (i) Y^+_infinity = 0; (ii) p does not divide h_n^+ for any n >= 1; (iii) E^+_{infinity,1}/C^+_{infinity,1} = 0. Proof. By (13.2), we deduce that p does not divide h_n^+ if and only if Y_n^+ = 0. (i) By Proposition 13.15, if p does not divide h_1^+, then 0 = Y_1^+ = (Y^+_infinity)_{Gamma_0^+} = 0. By Nakayama's lemma, this implies that Y^+_infinity = 0. (ii) Combining (i) with Proposition 13.15 shows Y_n^+ = 0, hence the result.
sources.match: Gives the two-step Nakayama argument explicitly.

nodes.title: The Vandiver hypothesis and the collapse of the four-term sequence to an isomorphism
nodes.statement: Define h_n^+ = #Cl(F_n^+) and say p is a VANDIVER PRIME if p does not divide h_1^+. THEOREM 13.11: if p is a Vandiver prime then there is an ISOMORPHISM of Lambda(Gamma^+)-modules X_infinity^+ = Lambda(Gamma^+)/I(Gamma^+)_{zeta_p}; in particular Iwasawa's Main Conjecture holds. The mechanism is COROLLARY 13.16: under the Vandiver hypothesis, (i) Y_infinity^+ = 0, (ii) p does not divide h_n^+ for any n >= 1, and (iii) E_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ = 0, where (iii) is proved using the finite-level cyclotomic-unit index [V_n^+ : D_n^+] = h_n^+ of Thm. 11.7, which is prime to p by (ii). Substituting (i) and (iii) into the four-term sequence of Cor. 13.14 collapses it to U_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ = X_infinity^+, and the Coleman-map computation of the left-hand side (their Thm. 12.23) gives the stated isomorphism. THE UNCONDITIONAL STATEMENT IS WEAKER: Thm. 13.8 asserts only the equality of IDEALS ch_{Lambda(Gamma^+)}(X_infinity^+) = I(Gamma^+)_{zeta_p}, and the module isomorphism of Thm. 13.11 is NOT asserted without Vandiver.
hypotheses: Vandiver's hypothesis is p not dividing h_1^+, i.e. the class number of the FIRST layer F_1^+, not of F^+ = Q(mu_p)^+ alone; Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams define it at level 1 and the equivalence with the usual formulation passes through Cor. 13.16(ii)
Vandiver's hypothesis is NOT known for all p; Thm. 13.11 is therefore conditional
the collapse needs BOTH Y_infinity^+ = 0 and E_{infinity,1}^+ = C_{infinity,1}^+; either one alone leaves a four-term or three-term sequence
step (iii) uses the finite-level index formula [V_n^+ : D_n^+] = h_n^+, which is an independent theorem (their Thm. 11.7) and belongs to the index-formula stage
the conclusion is a MODULE ISOMORPHISM, strictly stronger than the ideal equality of Thm. 13.8
proofSteps: By (13.2), p not dividing h_n^+ is equivalent to Y_n^+ = 0; the Vandiver hypothesis gives this at n = 1.
The control statement plus Nakayama gives Y_infinity^+ = 0, and then Y_n^+ = 0 for all n.
The index formula [V_n^+ : D_n^+] = h_n^+ is then prime to p, from which (iii) follows.
Substituting into Cor. 13.14 gives U_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ = X_infinity^+, and the local-unit computation identifies the left-hand side with Lambda(Gamma^+)/I(Gamma^+)_{zeta_p}.
acceptance: Check that the unconditional theorem is the IDEAL equality (Thm. 13.8) and that the isomorphism requires Vandiver; asserting the isomorphism unconditionally would be an unjustified strengthening.
Check that the collapse uses both vanishing statements from Cor. 13.16.
Check the index formula input [V_n^+ : D_n^+] = h_n^+ and that it is Thm. 11.7, proved independently of the main conjecture.
Check that the local-unit identification is a statement about LOCAL units and does not by itself give the Galois-theoretic conclusion.

nodes.title: Generalised Ritter-Weiss modules, the conditions (A1)-(A5) and the quadratic presentation
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, H/F finite abelian with G = Gal(H/F), S_infinity the archimedean places of F and S_ram the finite places ramifying in H. Let Sigma, Sigma' be DISJOINT finite sets of places of F satisfying (A1) Sigma union Sigma' contains S_infinity union S_ram, and (A2) the torsion subgroup of O^*_{H,S_infinity,Sigma'} = {u in O_H^* : u congruent to 1 (mod q) for all primes q above primes in Sigma'} is TRIVIAL. Then there is a Z[G]-module nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H), generalising the construction of Ritter-Weiss (which did not consider the smoothing set Sigma') and the authors' own earlier work (which imposed the additional condition Sigma contains S_infinity), sitting in a short exact sequence of Z[G]-modules 0 -> Cl^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) -> nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) -> X_{H,Sigma} -> 0, where X_{H,Sigma} is the group of degree-zero divisors on the places of H above Sigma and Cl^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) is the Sigma-depleted, Sigma'-smoothed class group. Now specialise: F totally real, H a CM field, c in G the complex conjugation, Z[G]^- = Z[G]/(1+c) -- which is FINITE FREE over Z and in particular TORSION FREE -- and M_- = M tensor_{Z[G]} Z[G]^- = M/(1+c)M. Impose further (A3) Sigma nonempty, (A4) Sigma contains {v in S_ram : v divides p}, (A5) Sigma' contains {v in S_ram : v does not divide p}. Under (A1)-(A5) the module nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H)_{p,-} = nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) tensor_{Z[G]} Z_p[G]^- is QUADRATICALLY PRESENTED over Z_p[G]^-, hence its Fitting ideal is PRINCIPAL.
hypotheses: Sigma and Sigma' must be DISJOINT; (A1) requires only their union to contain S_infinity union S_ram, so neither alone need contain the archimedean places -- this is precisely the generalisation over the authors' earlier work, which required Sigma to contain S_infinity
(A2) is a genuine torsion-freeness condition on the Sigma'-smoothed units, not a formality

for the minus construction, Z[G]^- is defined as the QUOTIENT Z[G]/(1+c), not as an eigenspace and not as the image of an idempotent; at p = 2 the minus quotient, the minus eigensubmodule and an integral idempotent summand are NOT the same object, and the source uses the quotient throughout
(A4) and (A5) split S_ram at p: the p-adic ramified places go into Sigma and the prime-to-p ramified places into Sigma'
the quadratic presentation -- and hence the principality of the Fitting ideal -- is a theorem under (A1)-(A5), not part of the definition
proofSteps: Construct nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) as in the source's Sec. 4 (the Ritter-Weiss complex, its global and local pieces, and the quadratic presentation of Sec. 4.5); that construction was NOT read here, only its output.
The short exact sequence relating the depleted-smoothed class group, nabla and the degree-zero divisor group is the structural statement quoted in the introduction.
The quadratic presentation over Z_p[G]^- is asserted under (A1)-(A5) and is what makes the Fitting ideal principal.
acceptance: Check that Sigma and Sigma' are disjoint and that only their UNION is required to contain S_infinity union S_ram.
Check the p = 2 warning: Z[G]^- is a quotient. Any argument that treats it as an eigenspace or as e^- Z[G] needs 2 inverted.
Check (A2) in the intended application; the Deligne-Ribet condition on T in Thm. 1.1 is a different condition and serves a different purpose (integrality of L_{S,T}(chi,0)).
Check that the principality of the Fitting ideal is derived from the quadratic presentation and is not assumed.

sources.excerpt: Let Sigma, Sigma' denote disjoint finite sets of places of F satisfying the following conditions: (A1) Sigma union Sigma' contains S_infinity union S_ram. (A2) The torsion subgroup of O^*_{H,S_infinity,Sigma'} = {u in O_H^* : u congruent to 1 (mod q) for all primes q above primes in Sigma'} is trivial. We will define a Z[G]-module nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) that generalizes the construction of Ritter-Weiss [23] (which did not consider the smoothing set Sigma') and our previous work [11] (which imposed an additional condition Sigma contains S_infinity). The module nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) sits in a short exact sequence of Z[G]-modules 0 -> Cl^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) -> nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H) -> X_{H,Sigma} -> 0.
sources.match: Gives (A1), (A2), the two generalisations over earlier constructions, and the defining short exact sequence.

sources.excerpt: Assume that F is totally real and that H is a CM field. Denote by c in G the complex conjugation, and define Z[G]^- = Z[G]/(1 + c). Note that Z[G]^- is finite free as a Z-module and in particular has no torsion. For any Z[G]-module M, we define M_- = M tensor_{Z[G]} Z[G]^- = M/(1 + c)M. Fix a prime p. We impose the further conditions (A3) Sigma nonempty. (A4) Sigma contains {v in S_ram : v | p}. (A5) Sigma' contains {v in S_ram : v does not divide p}.
sources.match: Gives the minus construction as a QUOTIENT, its freeness over Z, and the three further conditions.

sources.excerpt: Under conditions (A1)-(A5), we prove that nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H)_{p,-} is quadratically presented over Z_p[G]^-, and hence that its Fitting ideal is principal.
sources.match: Gives the quadratic presentation and the consequent principality.

nodes.title: The keystone Fitting-ideal theorem over Z, its one-half normalisation, and the Brumer-Stark conclusion
nodes.statement: THEOREM 1.2 (Dasgupta-Kakde-Silliman-Wang): under conditions (A1)-(A5), Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(H)_{p,-}) = (Theta^{Sigma'}_Sigma/2^t), where t = #(S_infinity intersect Sigma') and Theta^{Sigma'}_Sigma/2^t is the UNIQUE element of Z_p[G]^- with chi(Theta^{Sigma'}_Sigma/2^t) = L_{Sigma,Sigma'}(chi^{-1},0)/2^t for all ODD characters chi of G. Its existence in (c-1)/2 . Z_p[G], and hence in Z_p[G]^-, follows from the Deligne-Ribet congruence together with an argument of Kurihara. The theorem was already proved for p ODD in the authors' earlier work, so the content here is the case p = 2; most of the arguments are given for all p. THEOREM 1.1 (the Brumer-Stark conjecture) is deduced: assume S contains S_infinity and S_ram, and that T satisfies the Deligne-Ribet condition ensuring the integrality of L_{S,T}(chi,0) -- namely T contains two primes of different residue characteristic, or one prime of residue characteristic larger than n + 1. Let p be a prime of F not in S union T that splits completely in H, and fix a prime P of H above p. Then there exists u in H^* with (i) |u|_w = 1 for all places w of H not above p, INCLUDING THE COMPLEX PLACES; (ii) sum over sigma in G of chi(sigma) ord_{sigma^{-1}(P)}(u) = L_{S,T}(chi,0) for all characters chi of G; and (iii) u congruent to 1 modulo q O_H for all q in T. KURIHARA'S Thm. 2.12 packages the same input in the (S,T) normalisation: if S contains S_ram(K/k) and (O^T_{K,S})^x is Z-torsion free, then Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(nabla^T_S(K)_{p,-}) = theta^T_{K/k,S} Z_p[G]^- and Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(Sel^T_S(K)_{p,-}) = (theta^T_{K/k,S})^# Z_p[G]^-.
hypotheses: the normalisation carries the explicit divisor 2^t with t = #(S_infinity intersect Sigma'); this is the archimedean minus correction and it is NOT a harmless unit at p = 2
the element Theta^{Sigma'}_Sigma/2^t is characterised by its values at ODD characters only

Theorem 1.1's hypotheses on T are the Deligne-Ribet condition (two primes of different residue characteristic, or one of residue characteristic > n+1); this is what makes L_{S,T}(chi,0) integral and is separate from (A1)-(A5)
condition (i) of Thm. 1.1 includes the COMPLEX places; the usual Brumer-Stark statement over Z requires this and it is stated explicitly

Kurihara's Thm. 2.12 requires S to contain S_ram(K/k) and (O^T_{K,S})^x to be Z-TORSION FREE, and its two displayed equations are EQUIVALENT: if A is a relation matrix of nabla^T_S(K)_p then (A-transpose)^# is a relation matrix of Sel^T_S(K)_p, so it suffices to prove the first
the passage from the keystone pair (Sigma, Sigma') to the pair (S,T) is not formal: Kurihara records that it uses the argument in the proof of Lemma 6 of a separate Dasgupta-Kakde-Silliman-Wang paper
proofSteps: The authors reduce Thm. 1.2 to the construction of a triple (T-tilde, phi, rho) with certain properties, after establishing in their Sec. 2.5 the 'important and surprisingly delicate' result that an INCLUSION in Thm. 1.2 already implies EQUALITY.
The Galois-representation input is the Hilbert-modular construction of their Sec. 3 (Hecke algebra, cusp form and homomorphism, Galois representation) together with Ribet's lemma in their Sec. 2.7.
The Ritter-Weiss complex and its quadratic presentation are constructed in their Sec. 4, and a duality theorem for class formations in their Sec. 5.

Kurihara deduces his Thm. 2.12 from the keystone theorem (7), Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(nabla^{Sigma'}_Sigma(K)_{p,-}) = theta^{Sigma'}_{K/k,Sigma} Z_p[G]^-, proved by Dasgupta-Kakde for p > 2 and by Dasgupta-Kakde-Silliman-Wang for p = 2, by changing (Sigma,Sigma') to (S,T). He also notes that the minus part of the equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture for K/k implies Thm. 2.12.
acceptance: Check the 2^t normalisation and the definition of t; a statement without it is not this theorem.

Check that Thm. 1.2 for p odd is the earlier result and that the new content is p = 2; the residually indistinguishable case that arises there is not covered by a theorem assuming distinct residual characters.
Check the Deligne-Ribet condition on T separately from (A1)-(A5).
Check that the inclusion-implies-equality step is a theorem (Sec. 2.5) and not a formality.
Check Kurihara's transpose argument: the two Fitting-ideal statements are equivalent via (A-transpose)^#, so proving one suffices; the sharp symbol is the involution and must be tracked.

Here Theta^{Sigma'}_Sigma/2^t denotes the unique element of Z_p[G]^- such that chi(Theta^{Sigma'}_Sigma/2^t) = L_{Sigma,Sigma'}(chi^{-1}, 0)/2^t (4) for all odd characters chi in G-hat.

sources.excerpt: Assume now that S contains the set S_infinity of real places and the set S_ram of finite primes ramifying in H. Assume that T satisfies the Deligne-Ribet condition ensuring the integrality of L_{S,T}(chi, 0), namely that T contains two primes of different residue characteristic, or one prime of residue characteristic larger than n + 1. Theorem 1.1 (Brumer-Stark Conjecture). Let p not in S union T be a prime of F that splits completely in H. Fix a prime P of H above p. There exists an element u in H^* satisfying the following. We have |u|_w = 1 for all places w of H not lying above p, including the complex places. We have sum_{sigma in G} chi(sigma) ord_{sigma^{-1}(P)}(u) = L_{S,T}(chi, 0) for all characters chi : G -> C^*. We have u congruent to 1 (mod q O_H) for all q in T.

In fact, if A = (a_{ij}) is a relation matrix of nabla^T_S(K)_p as a Z_p[G]-module, (tA)^# = (a^#_{ji}) becomes a relation matrix of Sel^T_S(K)_p.

nodes.title: The complex RGamma_c(O_{F_infinity,S}, Z_p(1)) and Kurihara's Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: Let k be totally real, F/k finite abelian and totally real, F_infinity/F cyclotomic, K = F(mu_{2p}), K_infinity = F_infinity(mu_{2p}) = F(mu_{p^infinity}), Delta = Gal(K_infinity/F_infinity) and Delta' = Gal(K/F) generated by the complex conjugation rho, so that K/F is quadratic after the normalising reduction F = K^+. For a Delta'-module M put M_- = M/(1+rho). Define Sel^T_S(K_infinity)_p as the projective limit of the Sel^T_S(K_n)_p along the norm maps, and Sel_S(K_infinity)_p similarly. There is a distinguished triangle RGamma_c(O_{K_infinity,S}, Z_p) -> RGamma_{c,T}(O_{K_infinity,S}, Z_p) -> (direct sum over w in T_{K_infinity} of Q_p/Z_p(1))^dual[-2] ->, whose first two complexes have second cohomology Sel_S(K_infinity)_p and Sel^T_S(K_infinity)_p and third cohomology (Q_p/Z_p(1))^dual and 0 respectively; hence there is an exact sequence (12) 0 -> Sel_S(K_infinity)_p -> Sel^T_S(K_infinity)_p -> direct sum over w in T_{K_infinity} of Z_p(-1) -> Z_p(-1) -> 0. LEMMA 4.2: (1) for p > 2 there is an isomorphism of Lambda_{F_infinity}-modules (Sel_S(K_infinity)_p)_-(1) = X_{F_infinity,S}; FOR p = 2 there is only a natural INJECTIVE homomorphism (Sel_S(K_infinity)_p)_-(1) -> X_{F_infinity,S} WHOSE COKERNEL IS OF ORDER 2. (2) Fitt_{Lambda_{F_infinity}}((Sel^T_S(K_infinity)_p)_-(1)) = (product over v in T of (1 - Frob_v)) g_{F_infinity/k,S} Lambda_{F_infinity}.
hypotheses: S is taken to contain the archimedean places, the places over p and the ramified places, and T as in Kurihara's Thm. 2.12

the reduction to the case F = K^+ with K/F quadratic is legitimate because Gal(F_infinity/k) splits as a finite abelian group times Z_p, so one may choose F' with F_infinity = F' k_infinity and F' intersect k_infinity = k and replace F by F'; and because g_{M_infinity/k,S} is the image of g_{F_infinity/k,S} under restriction, so the equality descends to every intermediate field

the p = 2 statement is NOT an isomorphism: the cokernel is a finite group of order 2, equivalently there is a Z/2 kernel on the dual side. This is a FINITE Z/2 correction, not a free Z_2-module, and it must be carried through before any height-one localisation discards it
the p > 2 proof uses H^i(Delta', Q_p/Z_p) = 0 for i >= 1; at p = 2 one has instead H^1(Delta', Q_p/Z_p) = Z/2Z and H^2(Delta', Q_p/Z_p) = 0, which is exactly the source of the order-2 discrepancy
the Tate twist (1) in Lemma 4.2 is part of the statement; the identification is between (Sel_S)_-(1) and X_{F_infinity,S}, not between the untwisted modules
proofSteps: Proposition 2.11 identifies the Pontryagin dual of Sel_S(K_infinity)_p with H^1_et(O_{K_infinity,S}, Q_p/Z_p(1)) = H^1(Gal(L_S/K_infinity), Q_p/Z_p(1)) for L_S/K_infinity the maximal extension unramified outside S.

For p > 2, the minus part of that dual is H^1(Gal(L_S/K_infinity), Q_p/Z_p)^{rho = -1} = H^1(Gal(L_S/K_infinity), Q_p/Z_p)^{Delta'}(1) = H^1(Gal(L_S/F_infinity), Q_p/Z_p)(1) = Hom(X_{F_infinity,S}, Q_p/Z_p)(1), using H^i(Delta', Q_p/Z_p) = 0 for i >= 1; dualising again gives (1).
For p = 2 the same inflation-restriction argument leaves a Z/2, because H^1(Delta', Q_p/Z_p) = Z/2Z while H^2(Delta', Q_p/Z_p) = 0.

Part (2) follows from Thm. 2.12 together with the exact sequence (12) and the definition of g_{F_infinity/k,S} as the image of tau(theta^#_{K_infinity/k,S}) under the restriction Q(Lambda_{K_infinity}) -> Q(Lambda_{F_infinity}).

Check the exact sequence (12): it has FOUR terms and ends in Z_p(-1), not in zero after three terms.

sources.excerpt: Since Gal(F_infinity/k) is a direct product of a finite abelian group of order prime to p and a finitely generated Z_p-module of rank 1, it is a direct product of a finite abelian group and Z_p. Therefore, we can take a subfield F' contained in F_infinity such that F_infinity = F' k_infinity and F' intersect k_infinity = k where k_infinity/k is the cyclotomic Z_p-extension. ... If we prove the equality in Theorem 4.1 for F_infinity/k, then for any intermediate field M of F/k and its cyclotomic Z_p-extension M_infinity, we can get the equality in Theorem 4.1 for M_infinity/k since g_{M_infinity/k,S} is the image of g_{F_infinity/k,S} under the natural restriction map. Therefore, in order to prove Theorem 4.1, we may assume that F = K^+, the maximal totally real subfield of K.

The second cohomology of the first two complexes are Sel_S(K_infinity)_p, Sel^T_S(K_infinity)_p, respectively ... and the third cohomology of them are (Q_p/Z_p(1))^dual, 0, respectively. It follows that we have an exact sequence 0 -> Sel_S(K_infinity)_p -> Sel^T_S(K_infinity)_p -> direct sum over w in T_{K_infinity} of Z_p(-1) -> Z_p(-1) -> 0. (12)

nodes.title: Kurihara's equivariant Iwasawa main conjecture Det(RGamma_c)^{-1} = g Lambda, including p = 2
nodes.statement: Let k be totally real, F/k finite abelian and totally real, F_infinity/F the cyclotomic Z_p-extension, and S a finite set of places containing the archimedean places, the places over p and the ramified places. Let Det denote the determinant functor from the category of perfect torsion complexes over Lambda_{F_infinity} to Q(Lambda_{F_infinity}), and let g_{F_infinity/k,S} be the image of tau(theta^#_{K_infinity/k,S}) under the restriction map Q(Lambda_{K_infinity}) -> Q(Lambda_{F_infinity}). THEOREM 4.1 (Equivariant Iwasawa Main Conjecture): Det(RGamma_c(O_{F_infinity,S}, Z_p(1)))^{-1} = g_{F_infinity/k,S} Lambda_{F_infinity}. The equality can equivalently be formulated using K-groups. THE THEOREM INCLUDES p = 2. The base k is an ARBITRARY totally real field and F = k is permitted; the statement is not restricted to fields abelian over Q.
hypotheses: S contains S_infinity, the p-adic places and the ramified places; a different S changes both sides
the determinant is taken on the category of PERFECT TORSION complexes, so perfectness of RGamma_c(O_{F_infinity,S}, Z_p(1)) is part of the input (I.8)

the element g_{F_infinity/k,S} is obtained from the CM Stickelberger element theta_{K_infinity/k,S} by applying the sharp involution and the cyclotomic twist tau and then restricting; the involution and twist are part of the statement
the theorem holds at p = 2, where the comparison with the Selmer modules is only an injection with cokernel of order 2 (Lemma 4.2(1)); the proof must dispose of that finite correction
an equality of characters over a field of fractions is NOT this statement: the assertion is an equality of Lambda_{F_infinity}-modules, i.e. integral
proofSteps: Reduce to F = K^+ with K/F quadratic, using the splitting of Gal(F_infinity/k) and the compatibility of g under restriction (I.8).
Use the exact sequence (12) and Lemma 4.2(2) to compute the Fitting ideal of (Sel^T_S(K_infinity)_p)_-(1) in terms of g_{F_infinity/k,S} and the Euler factors at T.

Use Lemma 4.2(1) to pass to X_{F_infinity,S}; at p = 2 this step introduces the finite cokernel of order 2, which Kurihara disposes of because the relevant computation is at height one and the two sides differ by a finite module.

Since Theorem 4.1 is an equality of two invertible modules, it suffices to compare them after localisation at the relevant height-one primes; the exact sequence (12) and Lemma 4.2 show the two sides differ by a finite Lambda_{F_infinity}-module M, which is invisible after localisation.
Corollary 4.3 is then deduced from Theorem 4.1 by a standard argument.

Check that the base k is arbitrary totally real and that F = k is allowed; a statement restricted to abelian-over-Q fields is strictly weaker.
Check the involution and twist in the definition of g_{F_infinity/k,S}; a formulation without tau and the sharp operation is a different element.
Check the finite-level-to-Iwasawa transition and the descent back to Lambda_{F_infinity}: a characterwise identity over Q(Lambda_{F_infinity}) is not yet the integral statement.
